meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

Pretty conclusive. The company that sells that software says in its own guide not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have that printed in my bag. So what else do you have, Hale?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He wrote it over the weekend somewhere else and pasted it in. That's all a pasted edit shows, Hale.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong is a mistake, not misconduct. Whatever happens in this room, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's what an outline is for. And you haven't answered me on the quotation.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

A forty-minute timed piece from September against a take-home essay proves he does better with time, and five minutes after class proves he was put on the spot. I'll want the version history and your November 2 notes sent to me in writing.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. He'll do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and it's done and marked before his December 1 deadline. The quotation and everything else go in my email.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, November 12, after school. The zero comes off the day that mark goes in.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes, once it's in my inbox tonight, Hale.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want the zero removed when that mark is entered, the version history and your November 2 notes sent to me, and an answer on the misquoted line. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the mark entered before December 1, and she still wants that in writing tonight, the zero removed when the new mark goes in, and your documents on paper; that is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, reached before her 4:40 call.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own file and something she could check on the screen.
What cost ground: opening with the checker score and calling it conclusive, because it was the one thing she had come ready to tear apart.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said a seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is just a mistake, answer that directly before moving to the outline, so she has no unanswered point to carry into her email.
